title: Engine Oil Filter Housing — Bypass Indicator and Filter Condition Check
abstract: Scheduled check of the oil filter bypass indicator and the filter element condition, recording the indicator state before the housing is opened because opening it resets the evidence.

sections.purpose: This task records the state of the mechanical bypass indicator and examines the oil filter element, so that an impending bypass is found before unfiltered oil has been through the bearings.
sections.job_setup_note: The indicator records nothing by itself: once it is pushed back in, the fact that it had popped is lost. Read it and record it before anything else is touched, and before the cowl is fully opened if it can be seen through the access door. Do not do this task within one hour of engine shutdown; hot oil will scald.
sections.procedure: 1. WARNING: DO NOT OPEN THE OIL SYSTEM WITHIN ONE HOUR OF SHUTDOWN. THE OIL IS ABOVE ONE HUNDRED DEGREES AND THE SYSTEM IS PRESSURISED. 2. Open the fan cowls in zone 422 and fit both hold-open rods. 3. Read the bypass indicator on the upper face of the housing and record whether it has tripped, before touching anything else. 4. Where the indicator has tripped, record it as a finding and continue: the element must be examined and the reason established. 5. Reset the indicator with a push and confirm that it stays in. 6. Position a drain tray under the housing. 7. Release the housing cover and remove the filter element. CAUTION: THE ELEMENT HOLDS ABOUT A LITRE OF OIL. LOWER IT INTO THE TRAY AND DO NOT INVERT IT OVER THE COWL. 8. Examine the element for metal particles under good light, and where any are found, put them on a patch for laboratory analysis. 9. Examine the element pleats for collapse and for the tell-tale bright band that shows the bypass has been flowing. 10. Examine the seal in the housing and the mount link D7920120683140 for oil tracking. 11. Check the heat shield SAL498770-46 for security and for contact marks against the cowl latch VA570633-07. 12. Fit a new element and a new seal, and close the housing to the torque given. 13. Check the shroud 1237EO and the firewall panel 1EO before closing the cowls. 14. Do a ground run to idle and check for leaks, then re-read the indicator.
sections.close_out: Record the as-found indicator state, the element condition, any particle finding and the post-run indicator state. Where the indicator had tripped, do not release the aircraft until the reason is established. Send any particle patch to the laboratory with the engine serial number.

type_data.effectivity_note: Auran 7720 aircraft; steps 3 to 5 apply only to housings with the pop-out indicator

safety_precautions: Do not open the oil system within one hour of shutdown.
Wear oil-resistant gloves and eye protection.

title: Engine Oil Filter Housing — Bypass Indicator and Filter Condition Check

issue.reason: A recording line is added for the walk-around reading of the indicator and resetting it on the ramp is prohibited.

abstract: Scheduled check of the oil filter bypass indicator and the filter element condition, with the walk-around reading now recorded in its own line and the indicator left tripped until an engineer has seen it.

sections.purpose: This task records the state of the mechanical bypass indicator and examines the oil filter element, so that an impending bypass is found before unfiltered oil has been through the bearings. It also carries the recording line for the walk-around reading of the same indicator, because the walk-around item has nowhere else to write it down.
sections.job_setup_note: The indicator records nothing by itself: once it is pushed back in, the fact that it had popped is lost. Read it and record it before anything else is touched, and before the cowl is fully opened if it can be seen through the access door. The same applies on the ramp. The walk-around item introduced with the indicator asks the line engineer to look at it, and a tripped indicator found there is the only evidence that a bypass event happened on the previous sector: an indicator reset at the gate leaves nothing behind and the element will be changed on schedule as if nothing had occurred. Do not do this task within one hour of engine shutdown; hot oil will scald.

CAUTION: A TRIPPED INDICATOR FOUND AT THE WALK-AROUND IS NOT RESET ON THE RAMP UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES. IT IS LEFT TRIPPED, ENTERED IN THE TECHNICAL LOG AND RESET ONLY UNDER THIS TASK, WITH THE ELEMENT IN FRONT OF YOU. 3. Open the fan cowls in zone 422 and fit both hold-open rods. 4. Send any particle patch to the laboratory with the engine serial number.
